benchmark_evidence.observed: Explicit sharing of private drafts, inbox/conversation-based access, single-editor takeover and live editing visibility are documented. Foundly does not yet claim live co-editing or inbox access equivalence.

The documented draft-reply API uses drafts write scope and explicit conversation/channel references, private/shared modes, recipient lists and bounded attachments. This is benchmark evidence, not a Foundly implementation claim.

Front documents sender-only reply, reply-all and forwarding in existing or new conversations. Foundly currently proves internal source-bound draft preparation only, not these complete delivery/threading workflows.

capabilities.foundly_current: Owned drafts, templates, threads and preferences remain standalone. Draft sharing uses explicit owner/admin authority, a bounded tenant member search, current member status and current parent ACL for all retained revisions. Edits use revision preconditions. Restore creates a new draft revision, preserves current collaborators, binds idempotency to the actor/input and does not send. History survives encrypted restart and persistence failure rolls back draft, history, audit and receipt together. Legacy unversioned drafts retain a labelled baseline. Dashboard separates drafts from retained messages and treats unavailable, invalid or incomplete source contracts as unavailable. A 20,000-revision fixture resolves current parent ACL once per read/export, with no cross-request authorization cache. Production client handlers preserve revision preconditions across paginated history and do not redraw detached workspaces; simulated DOM tests do not establish browser acceptance. Reply/forward preparation now binds the exact retained message revision/hash, validates explicit recipients, creates only an unsent internal draft and never copies external source instructions into its body. Current source ownership/capabilities govern derived drafts and revision history; retained export still survives module disablement under the existing export permission and current source ownership. Drafts now retain bounded UTF-8 .txt attachments with exact byte hashes, private encrypted content storage, current parent/source ACL, CAS attach/detach, immutable historical references and restore, and owned export after module disablement. Attachment bytes are excluded from generic Data and ZERO projections; native client downloads validate the hash and use text/plain without inline rendering. No malware scan is claimed. A dedicated retained-message inbox now searches subject/body/participants with pagination, direction and personal read/archive filters. Unknown personal read state and external mailbox completeness remain explicit; changed source revisions invalidate old read evidence. Personal state is isolated per current user, revision-bound, audited, atomic and exportable under current source access. Native message detail is read-only, with separate draft preparation; opening a message never silently records it as read. Real sessions prove body-wait source changes/reownership, readonly denial and encrypted replay. Client handlers reject late search results and detached updates. Explicit read-only IMAP INBOX receipt now uses verified implicit TLS on 993, pinned public IPv4, AUTH PLAIN, EXAMINE and BODY.PEEK. Bounded UIDVALIDITY/UID scans retain exact encrypted MIME bytes with integrity-checked current-source downloads and owned export. Provider Draft flags never create internal drafts or count as recorded messages; later observed draft flags hide ordinary inbox/messages/snapshot and derived-source reads while labelled historical owned export remains. Missing/oversized/malformed content stays unavailable. Pagination, changed UID sets, atomic import rollback and current account/member revocation pass local TLS, unit, real HTTP/restart and production-handler fixtures. Scan coverage describes observed UIDs over a window, including excluded drafts; it is not a current external message count, identity proof or delivery receipt. No real provider account was accessed. Source-bound reply review now includes exact RFC 5322 In-Reply-To/References headers; source revision changes block review and submission. Approved submission persists the same linkage without claiming recipient delivery; forwards do not acquire reply headers. Current-source conversations derive only from visible retained headers, never subject equality, and expose duplicate-ID ambiguity, incomplete participants and unknown external coverage. Native HTTP, isolated approved-submission, encrypted restart and production DOM handlers pass. Malformed Reply-To is unavailable instead of silently selecting a different recipient. Provider Draft flags continue to withdraw ordinary message and derived-draft access.
capabilities.gap: Live co-editing/takeover, comments, reply-all, broader attachment formats and scanning, and richer provider inbox workflows remain incomplete. Read-only bounded INBOX receipt and header-derived threaded replies are implemented and locally verified. Actual browser/keyboard/viewport and legitimate account acceptance remain unproven.
capabilities.required_change: Complete collaborative, reply-all and broader attachment workflows; verify real browser and authorized provider behavior without changing this run’s production permissions.
capabilities.foundly_differentiator: Candidate: shared Core identity, provenance and ZERO tools. Comparative superiority is not proven.
